steps.html:
Forty questions on Chapters 10, 11 and 12 — the last quarter of the level. No time limit, feedback as you go, and you can retake it as often as you like.

  • 40 questions · pass mark 70%
  • Grammar from Lessons 37–48
  • Vocabulary from all three wordlists
  • Function and register

steps.title: Lesson 37 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Besides the schedule, what else did streaming remove?
options: the accident of finding something you were not looking for
advertisements, which no longer interrupt anything
the evening news everybody watched at the same time
steps.answer: the accident of finding something you were not looking for
steps.why: The loss the survey group could not name until asked differently.

steps.title: Lesson 38 · reporting verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She reminded me ___ him.'
steps.answer: to email
steps.why: Remind somebody to do something.

steps.title: Lesson 38 · reporting verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'He denied ___ her essay.'
steps.answer: copying
steps.why: Deny + -ing.

steps.title: Lesson 38 · reporting verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: She refused that she ate it.
steps.answer: She refused to eat it.
steps.why: Refuse to do.

steps.title: Lesson 38 · reporting verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'He invited me ___ to the concert.'
steps.answer: to come
steps.why: Invite somebody to do something.

steps.title: Lesson 38 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Three true, recent stories did not lead the news. What do they share?
options: None of them has a villain, and conflict is what carries a story to the front.
They were all about the same country.
steps.answer: None of them has a villain, and conflict is what carries a story to the front.
steps.why: A discovery, an act of honesty and a successful campaign all lack conflict.

steps.title: Lesson 39 · complex sentences
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The recommended way into a long sentence is to find …
options: the first comma and read up to it
the main verb, then the subject, then everything else
the longest noun phrase in the sentence
steps.answer: the main verb, then the subject, then everything else
steps.why: Everything else in the sentence hangs off the main clause.

steps.title: Lesson 39 · hedging
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'The company called the miners' chances unfortunate.' Quoting that single word shows …
options: that it is the most accurate word available
that it is conspicuously mild for what was being described
that it was the only public statement made
steps.answer: that it is conspicuously mild for what was being described
steps.why: The mildness tells you what the sentence was trying to do.

steps.title: Lesson 40 · distancing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'It took him six days, supposedly.' The speaker …
options: read it somewhere and is passing it on
is joking and does not believe it
steps.answer: read it somewhere and is passing it on
steps.why: Supposedly marks the source as second-hand.

steps.title: Lesson 40 · distancing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which reports a claim without endorsing it?
options: Rats eat each other when food runs out.
The ship was said to be carrying cannibal rats.
The ship was carrying cannibal rats.
steps.answer: The ship was said to be carrying cannibal rats.
steps.why: Be said to attributes the claim to somebody else.

steps.title: Lesson 40 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A story that grows as it is repeated and then gets reported as news is an example of …
steps.answer: a vicious circle
steps.why: Papers report, stories are shared and exaggerated, papers report the online version.

steps.title: Lesson 41 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Why does knowing something is an illusion not dissolve it?
options: because people forget what they were told beforehand
because the brain shows you the answer, not the working
because the image is too well made for the eye to argue with
steps.answer: because the brain shows you the answer, not the working
steps.why: The result does not change when you learn how it was produced.

steps.title: Lesson 43 · sense verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: I watched the news last night.
I looked the news last night.
I saw at the news last night.
steps.answer: I watched the news last night.
steps.why: Watch for something that unfolds over time and holds your attention.

steps.title: Lesson 43 · sense verbs
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Could you ___ at this for a moment?'
steps.answer: look
steps.why: Look at = direct your eyes deliberately.

steps.title: Lesson 43 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A dessert on a white plate tasted about ten per cent sweeter than on a black one. This implies that …
options: people cannot report what they taste
taste is assembled from several senses, so changing what is seen changes what is tasted
white plates should be used in all restaurants
steps.answer: taste is assembled from several senses, so changing what is seen changes what is tasted
steps.why: Nothing about the dessert changed, so taste alone was not producing the result.

steps.title: Lesson 44 · describing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which introduces a scene best?
options: I can see a man, and he seems to be doing something.
There's a man in the foreground, cooking something.
A man cooking, near the front of the picture.
steps.answer: There's a man in the foreground, cooking something.
steps.why: Place it first with there is; save the sense verbs for interpretation.

steps.title: Lesson 44 · hedging a description
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You are not certain what the object is. Which is best?
options: They're sitting in a rubber boat.
They're sitting in what looks like a rubber boat.
They're definitely in a rubber boat.
steps.answer: They're sitting in what looks like a rubber boat.
steps.why: What looks like marks the description as your interpretation.

steps.title: Lesson 44 · clarifying
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You did not catch one phrase. Which repair is most efficient?
options: Sorry, what do you mean by 'in the foreground'?
Could you say all of that again?
steps.answer: Sorry, what do you mean by 'in the foreground'?
steps.why: Naming the phrase means the other person repairs only that.

steps.title: Lesson 42 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The field's most reliable finding about humour is that …
options: wordplay travels between languages better than anything else
almost anything is funny if the audience does not see it coming
steps.answer: almost anything is funny if the audience does not see it coming
steps.why: Which is why a joke you have been told is coming cannot work.

steps.title: Lesson 45 · second conditional
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'If she ___ a second child, she would divide her time in half.'
steps.answer: had
steps.why: Second conditional: an unreal present.

steps.title: Lesson 45 · third conditional
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'If she ___ children, she wouldn't have had this life.'
steps.answer: had had
steps.why: Third conditional: an unreal past.

steps.title: Lesson 45 · mixed conditional
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'If I had grown up alone, I ___ a different person now.'
steps.answer: would be
steps.why: Mixed: a past condition with a present result.

steps.title: Lesson 45 · conditionals
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: If they had told us earlier, we could have rebooked.
If they would have told us earlier, we could have rebooked.
Had they told us earlier, we could have rebooked.
steps.answer: If they would have told us earlier, we could have rebooked.
steps.why: Would never goes in the if clause, however natural it sounds.

steps.title: Lesson 46 · wish
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I wish I ___ more time.'
steps.answer: had
steps.why: A present situation you want to be different takes the past simple.

steps.title: Lesson 46 · wish
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She wishes she ___ something at the time.'
steps.answer: had said
steps.why: A past regret takes the past perfect.

steps.title: Lesson 46 · wish
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: I wish I could remember his name.
I wish I would remember his name.
I wish they would remind me.
steps.answer: I wish I would remember his name.
steps.why: Wish + would is used about somebody else's behaviour, never your own.

steps.title: Lesson 46 · reading
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Over a lifetime people regret inactions more than actions because …
options: actions are simply more memorable than things never done
an inaction leaves a gap the imagination fills with the best version
people forget what they did not do, so it stops troubling them
steps.answer: an inaction leaves a gap the imagination fills with the best version
steps.why: The imagined version never has to compete with what actually happened.

steps.title: Lesson 47 · compound adjectives
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
steps.answer: a forty-minute delay
steps.why: The first element of a compound adjective stays singular.

steps.title: Lesson 47 · compound adjectives
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'glasses with thick rims' becomes …
steps.answer: thick-rimmed glasses
steps.why: The noun becomes a past participle.

steps.title: Lesson 47 · compound adjectives
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which describes a shirt made now in the style of the 1970s?
steps.answer: retro-style
steps.why: Retro-style: made now, in an older style. Second-hand means previously owned.

steps.title: Lesson 47 · vague language
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: '…music, clothes, books and stuff like that.' The phrase …
options: closes a list the speaker could have gone on with
corrects something the speaker just said
softens an opinion the speaker is unsure of
steps.answer: closes a list the speaker could have gone on with
steps.why: It signals there are more items and the speaker has stopped naming them.

steps.title: Lesson 48 · looking back
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which means 'it looked bad at the time and turned out well'?
options: It was a blessing in disguise.
steps.answer: It was a blessing in disguise.
steps.why: The other two are regret and acceptance.

steps.title: Lesson 48 · looking back
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'He would never have become Prime Minister ___ the war.'
steps.answer: if it weren't for
steps.why: If it weren't for + noun, for a single decisive factor.

steps.title: Lesson 48 · looking back
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which phrase accepts something that can no longer be changed?
steps.answer: What's done is done.
steps.why: The first is regret, the third is relief; only the second closes the question.

steps.title: Lessons 40 and 44 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which marks the statement as the speaker's interpretation?
options: The boat is about to crash.
It looks as if the boat is about to crash.
steps.answer: It looks as if the boat is about to crash.
steps.why: It looks as if is honest about a painting; the bare statement is not.

steps.title: Lessons 45 and 48 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which refuses to claim a result?
options: If he hadn't been born into that family, who knows?
steps.answer: If he hadn't been born into that family, who knows?
steps.why: It states the condition and declines the consequence.

steps.title: Chapters 10–12 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To worry continuously about small things is to …
steps.answer: fret
steps.why: Fret.

steps.title: Lesson 41 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Something that is not what it appears to be, although you know it, is …
steps.answer: an illusion
steps.why: An illusion. Allusion is an indirect reference.

steps.title: Lesson 42 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To rate a performance as extremely good you would call it …
steps.answer: outstanding
steps.why: Outstanding.

steps.title: Chapters 10–12 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Simple, and not using advanced technology, is …
steps.answer: low-tech
steps.why: Low-tech: record players, typewriters.

steps.title: Урок пройден
steps.sub: Block Test 4 · Lessons 37–48
items: I have tested the last quarter of the level.
I can use reporting verbs, conditionals and wish.
I can hedge, describe and clarify.
I know the vocabulary of Chapters 10–12.
